questions.question: ‘Ram Navami’ is celebrated in India to commemorate the:
questions.option_3: coronation ceremony of Lord Rama as a king.
questions.option_4: return of Lord Rama from forest.
questions.solution:
Ram Navami is a significant Hindu festival celebrated to commemorate the birth of Lord Rama, the seventh avatar of Lord Vishnu.
  • Significance: It marks the descent of divine light on earth and occurs on the ninth day (Navami) of the Chaitra month in the Hindu lunar calendar.
  • Celebration: Devotees observe fasts, recite the Ramayana, and perform 'Bhajans' and 'Kirtans'.
Note: While the return from the forest is celebrated as Diwali and the death of Ravana as Dussehra, Ram Navami specifically honors his birth in Ayodhya.

questions.question: For how many days is the Chhat Puja celebrated?
questions.solution:
Chhat Puja is an ancient Hindu Vedic festival dedicated to the Sun God (Surya) and his wife Usha (Chhathi Maiya), and it is celebrated for a total of four days.
  • Day 1 (Nahay Khay): Devotees take a holy dip in water and eat a single meal.
  • Day 2 (Lohanda and Kharna): A day-long fast is observed, broken only after sunset with Kheer and Puri.
  • Day 3 (Sandhya Arghya): Preparation of offerings (Thekua) and offering prayer to the setting sun.
  • Day 4 (Usha Arghya): Offering prayer to the rising sun, marking the conclusion of the fast.
Additional Info: It is primarily celebrated in Bihar, Jharkhand, and Uttar Pradesh.

questions.question: Madhavpur Fair in Gujarat is a _______ day long event to celebrate Lord Krishna's marriage with Rukmani.
questions.solution:
The Madhavpur Fair is a five-day long cultural event held in the village of Madhavpur Ghed in Gujarat.
  • Theme: It celebrates the mythological marriage of Lord Krishna and Princess Rukmani.
  • Cultural Connect: It creates a symbolic link between Western India (Gujarat) and Northeast India, as Rukmani is believed to have been from the Mishmi Tribe of present-day Arunachal Pradesh.
Note: The festival showcases folk dance, music, and local handicrafts reflecting the fusion of different Indian cultures.

questions.question: In which of the following states is the Mamallapuram Utsav celebrated?
questions.solution:
The Mamallapuram Utsav (also known as the Indian Dance Festival) is celebrated in the state of Tamil Nadu.
  • Venue: It is held against the backdrop of the iconic Shore Temple and the rock-cut sculptures of Mahabalipuram (a UNESCO World Heritage site).
  • Purpose: It promotes classical dances like Bharatanatyam, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, and Mohiniyattam.
Additional Note: The festival usually takes place during the months of January and February to promote tourism and heritage.

questions.question: In which neighbouring country of India is the Haa Summer Festival celebrated?
questions.solution:
The Haa Summer Festival is a vibrant and lively celebration held in Bhutan.
  • Location: It takes place in the picturesque Haa Valley.
  • Highlights: The festival celebrates the traditional nomadic lifestyles, local Bhutanese cuisine, and indigenous sports like archery and Khuru (darts).
  • Significance: It offers a glimpse into the lives and culture of the nomadic herders (Haaps) and pays tribute to nature and local deities.

questions.question: Which day is celebrated as International Day of Non-Violence?
questions.solution:
The International Day of Non-Violence is observed on 2nd October every year.
  • Reason: It coincides with the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi, the leader of the Indian independence movement and pioneer of the philosophy and strategy of non-violence.
  • Establishment: The United Nations General Assembly established this day in 2007 to spread the message of non-violence through education and public awareness.
Note: Gandhi’s philosophy of Ahimsa (non-violence) influenced civil rights movements globally.

questions.question: In which of the following states is the groundnut fair, ’Kadalekayi Parishe’ celebrated on the last Monday of the Karthika month of the Hindu calendar?
questions.solution:
Kadalekayi Parishe, also known as the Groundnut Fair, is an annual festival celebrated in Karnataka, specifically in Basavanagudi, Bengaluru.
  • Timing: It is held on the last Monday of Karthika Masa.
  • Tradition: Farmers offer their first harvest of groundnuts to the Bull Temple (Dodda Ganeshana Gudi) to seek blessings for a good yield.
  • History: Legend says a bull used to destroy groundnut crops, so farmers promised to offer their first harvest to appease the Bull (Nandi).

questions.question: Children’s Day in India is celebrated to commemorate the birth anniversary of _________.
questions.solution:
Children’s Day (Bal Diwas) in India is celebrated on November 14th to commemorate the birth anniversary of Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru.
  • Significance: Nehru, India's first Prime Minister, was known for his immense love and affection for children, who fondly called him ‘Chacha Nehru’.
  • Focus: The day emphasizes the rights, care, and education of children, whom Nehru considered the future of the nation.
Note: Globally, World Children's Day is observed on November 20th, but India shifted its celebration to November 14th after Nehru's death in 1964.

questions.question: Who among the following is/was a famous proponent of Bharatanatyam?
questions.solution:
Rukmini Devi Arundale was a renowned dancer and choreographer who is credited with the renaissance of Bharatanatyam.
  • Contribution: She helped transition the dance form from the Sadir (traditionally performed by Devadasis) to a respected global art form.
  • Legacy: She founded the Kalakshetra Foundation in Chennai, an institution dedicated to the preservation of traditional Indian values in art.
Additional Info: She was the first woman in Indian history to be nominated as a member of the Rajya Sabha.

questions.question: Who is revered as ‘Karnataka Sangeeta Pitamaha’?
questions.solution:
Purandara Dasa is revered as the 'Karnataka Sangeeta Pitamaha' (the Father/Grandsire of Carnatic Music).
  • Systematization: He formulated the basic lessons of Carnatic music, including the Sarali Varisai and Alankaras, which are still used by students today.
  • Compositions: He was a prolific composer who wrote thousands of Kirthanas (devotional songs) in Kannada and Sanskrit.
Note: He was a prominent member of the Haridasa movement and a devotee of Lord Vitthala.
